[Explanation] Akamai Signs $11.6 Billion Cloud Deal with Anthropic
U.S.-based Akamai Technologies has signed a seven-year, $11.6 billion cloud agreement with AI development leader Anthropic. This move reflects a structural shift in the industry, where securing decentralized computing infrastructure—independent of traditional single-cloud providers—has become essential to meet the explosively growing computational demands of AI models.
The Full Scope of the $11.6 Billion Mega-Deal Between Akamai and Anthropic
Overview of the Agreement and Key Highlights
On September 24, 2026, U.S. cloud giant Akamai Technologies announced that it had signed a seven-year, $11.6 billion (approximately 1.7 trillion yen) cloud infrastructure agreement with AI development leader Anthropic. This contract is one of the largest commercial transactions in Akamai's history, supporting Anthropic's surging CPU workloads and large-scale computational processing needs through Akamai's decentralized cloud platform, "Akamai Cloud." Furthermore, the agreement includes a contract expansion clause of up to $9 billion, potentially bringing the total transaction value to approximately $20 billion. Regarding the impact on financial performance, while there is no change to the full-year 2026 revenue guidance, service delivery is scheduled to begin sequentially from the second half of 2027. According to Dr. Tom Leighton, co-founder and CEO of Akamai, the company expects a revenue contribution of $150 million to $300 million in 2027, growing to an annual run rate of approximately $1.7 billion by 2028. Akamai had already secured over $2.8 billion in cloud infrastructure contracts in 2026, but this deal solidifies its position as an AI infrastructure provider.
Granting of Stock Warrants and Deep Collaboration in Both Capital and Business
An extremely unusual feature of this agreement is the strong capital tie-up accompanying the transaction. Akamai has granted Anthropic warrants (stock acquisition rights) for non-voting convertible Series B preferred stock, which can be converted into up to approximately 7.7 million shares of common stock (equivalent to about 5% of issued common shares) at an exercise price of $111.33 per share. Approximately 2% of the warrants vested immediately in connection with the initial $11.6 billion commitment, with the remaining 3% vesting in stages based on additional service purchases (approximately 1% for every $3 billion). This is the first time in Akamai's 28-year history that a cloud provider has issued stock warrants to a customer. CEO Tom Leighton stated that this is a meaningful step toward deepening the long-term, strategic partnership between the two companies. While market analysts have praised this capital alliance as a sign of high confidence in the sustainability of AI demand, there is also interest in the circular nature of the transaction, where AI companies and infrastructure firms hold each other's capital and business. The conceptual diagram below illustrates the transaction structure between the two companies.
Surging Demand for Generative AI and Structural Shift to Decentralized Infrastructure
Background of Anthropic's Explosive Growth and Securing Compute Resources
The backdrop to Anthropic's series of massive infrastructure deals is the staggering growth in demand for its "Claude" AI model. According to CEO Dario Amodei, the company's annualized revenue recorded an exceptional 80-fold year-on-year growth in the first quarter of 2026, reaching a run-rate revenue of $47 billion (approximately 7 trillion yen) as of May 2026. Additionally, in its Series H round in May 2026, the company raised $65 billion, pushing its valuation to $965 billion, nearly reaching the $1 trillion mark. With this rapid increase in usage, a severe shortage of computational resources has become a challenge, and the company has been scrambling to secure large-scale compute resources to maintain its model training and inference environments. In 2026, the company has been aggressively pursuing multi-billion dollar infrastructure procurement, including a $10 billion deal with Volta, a $13.7 billion deal with Lam Group, the leasing of the entire capacity of the Colossus 1 data center operated by xAI, and a partnership with Amazon (AWS) exceeding $100 billion and 5 gigawatts.
Breaking Away from Dependence on Traditional Hyperscalers and Moving Toward Multi-Cloud
Anthropic's infrastructure procurement strategy marks a clear departure from the "dependence on a specific single hyperscaler" seen in traditional frontier AI development companies. The company has now built a multi-provider system combining the "Big Three"—Amazon (AWS), Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure—along with xAI's Colossus 1 and Akamai. In particular, the adoption of Akamai, which possesses over 4,300 edge locations in 135 countries worldwide, enables low-latency inference processing and distributed execution of CPU workloads in edge environments scattered across the globe. Especially in enterprise sectors with high regulatory requirements such as law, finance, and healthcare, it is necessary to meet data residency (restrictions on data storage regions) and cybersecurity requirements, where Akamai's decentralized infrastructure plays a crucial role. This multi-cloud structure, which allows for business continuity even if a single massive cloud experiences outages or regulatory changes, has become a source of competitive advantage in the enterprise AI market.
Ripple Effects on the Entire Industry and the Future of AI Infrastructure
Stock Market Evaluation and Akamai's Large-Scale Capital Expenditure Plan
Following the announcement of the mega-deal, the stock market reacted very favorably to Akamai's business transformation. In after-hours trading immediately following the announcement, Akamai's stock price (AKAM) surged by 20% to 22%, jumping from its previous level of $110.41 to around $133.50. Akamai had been forced to endure 17 consecutive quarters of declining revenue in its core content delivery (CDN) business due to major customers bringing services in-house and intensifying competition, but the market has now re-evaluated the company from a "mature CDN firm" to a "growth company in large-scale AI infrastructure." To fulfill the contract, Akamai expects capital expenditure (CapEx) of approximately $5.5 billion against the initial $11.6 billion commitment. For 2026 alone, the company raised its capital expenditure forecast by approximately $1.7 billion to pre-purchase critical components such as memory, issued a $1.7 billion construction request to major electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider Jabil, and completed a hardware procurement agreement with Lenovo. Physical infrastructure construction is already well underway.
The Rise of Edge-Based AI Computing Platforms and Future Outlook
This agreement symbolizes the arrival of a major trend in the future AI infrastructure market: "from centralized data centers to edge-distributed computing platforms." With the spread of agentic AI that autonomously executes inferences and tasks, demand for low-latency processing at network endpoints and distributed computing with high CPU loads is expected to increase further. The biggest point of focus for future developments is the pace of progress in service delivery and monetization, which will begin in earnest from the second half of 2027. The focus will be on whether Akamai can smoothly achieve its target annual revenue run rate of $1.7 billion by 2028, and whether the additional $9 billion contract expansion option will be exercised. Furthermore, the latest developments at Anthropic, which is rumored to be planning an initial public offering (IPO), and the expansion of multi-cloud AI usage by enterprise customers will also be important evaluation axes. As the fusion of centralized hyperscalers and decentralized edge clouds progresses, the horizon of AI infrastructure is entering a new phase of growth.

Akamai Technologies issues warrant to Anthropic for 5% of common stock in massive cloud deal
The cloud infrastructure provider is betting big on AI workloads with an $11.6 billion commitment and a unique equity arrangement that ties ownership to spending milestones.
Akamai Technologies just handed Anthropic the keys to a potentially enormous equity stake, issuing a warrant that lets the AI company purchase up to 5% of Akamai’s common stock. The catch: Anthropic has to spend billions on Akamai’s cloud services to fully unlock it.
The warrant is part of an $11.6 billion deal spanning seven years, announced on September 24, in which Akamai will provide cloud infrastructure to support Anthropic’s growing AI workload demands. Combined with a previous $1.8 billion contract announced in May, the total potential value of the relationship sits at roughly $20 billion.
Akamai structured the warrant around non-voting convertible Series B Preferred Stock, representing approximately 7.7 million shares of common stock. The exercise price is set at $111.33 per share.
About 2% of Akamai’s common stock vests immediately upon the $11.6 billion commitment. The remaining 3% vests incrementally as Anthropic spends up to an additional $9 billion on Akamai’s services over the contract’s duration.
The “non-voting” designation matters too. Anthropic can benefit financially from Akamai’s stock appreciation without gaining any boardroom influence. Akamai keeps control of its corporate governance while still offering a meaningful financial incentive to its largest client.
The bigger picture: $20 billion in combined contracts
Anthropic will use Akamai Cloud specifically for scaling CPU workloads, with revenue recognition kicking in as capacity gets activated.

For Akamai, a company historically known for content delivery networks and cybersecurity, landing a deal of this magnitude represents a serious pivot toward AI infrastructure.
What this means for Akamai’s competitive position
Akamai has historically competed in a different weight class than the hyperscale cloud giants. Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud dominate enterprise cloud spending, and all three have their own AI partnerships and internal AI efforts. AWS, notably, has invested billions into Anthropic directly.
Akamai’s annual revenue has historically hovered in the low single-digit billions, so a seven-year deal worth $11.6 billion, with potential upside to $20 billion, represents a transformational shift.
If Anthropic fully vests and exercises its 5% stake at $111.33 per share, that represents roughly $857 million in potential equity value at the exercise price alone.
For Akamai shareholders, the dilution is the obvious trade-off. Issuing up to 7.7 million new shares to a single customer is not trivial. But the argument from Akamai’s perspective is straightforward: 5% dilution is a reasonable price for locking in a customer that could eventually account for a significant portion of total revenue.

Akamai’s (AKAM) Latest Move Has Jim Cramer Thinking Differently
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 9:02 AM PDT 5 min read
On October 1, Jim Cramer discussed Akamai Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ:AKAM) on Mad Money, highlighting its distributed computing plans and recently announced agreement with Anthropic.
Previously, Cramer called the company "terrific" and mentioned another one of his favorite companies.
Cramer introduced Akamai Technologies, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:AKAM) approach to AI infrastructure, as he said:
Next, there's Akamai. Now, late last year, they announced a new initiative, Akamai Inference Cloud, which is basically a network of many smaller data centers spread across the globe that help these AI models process data. Management figures that we're moving from a period of training AI models to a world where we actually use these models at scale, and that requires a lot more infrastructure. Now, in early August, we had Akamai CEO Dr. Tom Leighton on the show for the first time in over five years. I'm going to let him explain what his company's trying to do.
Cramer's segment included Leighton's explanation:
We're unique in being able to support the AI infrastructure needs from core to edge so that whatever task you have, whatever agent you're working with or model, if you need to train it, okay, maybe we do that in the core. But the real usage, the day-to-day use is inference where that model is being queried, it's telling a robot to do something. And that you want to do close to the robot or close to the user so it's fast and scales and is efficient.
Akamai's Cloud Infrastructure Services revenue increased 39% year-over-year to approximately $99 million in the second quarter. Security revenue rose 10% to approximately $604 million, helping total revenue grow 5% to approximately $1.1 billion.
Cramer explained why the distributed approach appealed to him, as he said:
Ever since that interview, I've been thinking a lot about this Akamai plan. First, it makes total sense. You need distributed data centers, especially as we get into things like this physical AI because this requires a lot of bandwidth and you want the infrastructure as close to the user as possible. That reduces latency... Plus, lately, we've seen massive central AI data centers become politically toxic, and it strikes me that Akamai's idea of building smaller data centers, that could be an easier sale, don't you think?
You can also read more on Cramer discussing the company's cloud pivot and robotics win.
Jim Cramer Says the Chip Shortage “Can’t Be Solved” Without KLAC
On September 24, Akamai Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ:AKAM) announced an approximately $11.6 billion agreement supporting Anthropic's central processing unit workloads. The arrangement also provides for a potential additional $9 billion in business, beyond the initial commitment. Cramer discussed the investment required and the size of the contract, as he said:
Now, this is an investment year for Akamai… They got to acquire and build the infrastructure for their inference cloud which will translate into a meaningful earnings hit. But management says there's a ton of customer interest here and they expect business to turn up in the fourth quarter before really booming in 2027. Hey, by the way, last Thursday, Akamai announced this big win with Anthropic for 11.6 billion contractual commitment over seven years. Clearly, Anthropic needs this additional capacity and they're willing to pay for it. This works out, by the way, to 1.66 billion per year. Pretty impressive given that it's more than a third of what Akamai is expected to bring in this year.
The annual figure Cramer mentioned is a simple average. Akamai's filing specifies separate seven-year project terms beginning on their respective service start dates, with payments subject to delivery and availability requirements. It does not establish equal annual revenue.
It trades at approximately 16.6x forward earnings, below Fastly's approximately 48x multiple. That offers relative valuation support, although the companies have different growth profiles and business mixes.
Spending Comes Before the Full Revenue Contribution
Akamai Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ:AKAM) estimates approximately $5.5 billion in capital expenditures related to the Anthropic commitment, including an additional approximately $1.7 billion in 2026. The announcement left its 2026 revenue guidance unchanged. The company also issued an Anthropic warrant covering up to approximately 5% of its outstanding common stock, with vesting linked to commitments and further expansion.
Execution remains important because the agreement allows termination for certain breaches and material outages. Existing operations also face pressure. Second-quarter delivery and other cloud applications revenue declined 6%, while adjusted earnings per share fell 8% to $1.59.
Short Interest Stays High as Hedge Fund Ownership Falls
According to Insider Monkey, 62 hedge funds held Akamai in the second quarter, compared with 74 in the prior quarter. Of those funds, Point72 Asset Management was the top shareholder and reduced its position by 22% to nearly 2.6 million shares. Short interest represented 15.37% of the public float, indicating substantial bearish positioning. The quarterly holdings predate the Anthropic announcement and do not show how funds responded to that agreement.
Despite the spending requirements, Cramer viewed the stock's retreat as an opportunity, as he commented:
Initially, the stock spiked in response as it should. But now it's given back all of those gains and then some. Well, that feels like a buying opportunity to me… So, have you missed it or can… [it] keep running?... Akamai, I think you can buy that stock right here, right now because it's cheap, selling for less than 16 times this year's earnings estimates, and you're basically getting the latest Anthropic partnership, which I thought was gigantic, for free. Sure, they're having a down year because of all that spending that I mentioned, but that's about to take a turn for the better real soon.
While we acknowledge the potential of AKAM as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. Akamai Stock Soars 20% After Anthropic Signs Massive Computing Deal
Akamai signs an $11.6 billion, seven year computing deal with Anthropic, sending shares up as much as 20% in after hours trading.
By Trader EdgeSeptember 25, 20263 Mins Read
Akamai signed an $11.6 billion, seven year contract with Anthropic for computing power

Akamai shares jumped as much as 20% in after hours trading

Akamai Technologies has signed a large computing contract with Anthropic. The deal is worth $11.6 billion and runs for seven years.
ANTHROPIC SIGNS $11.6B AKAMAI CLOUD DEAL
Anthropic has committed $11.6B over seven years to use Akamai $AKAM infrastructure for growing CPU workloads, with options to expand the relationship by another $9B, bringing the potential total to ~$20B.

The agreement will supply Anthropic with central processing units. These are general purpose chips used to help run AI software.
Akamai shares jumped as much as 20% in after hours trading following the news. The stock rose to roughly $129.60 per share.
This is the largest deal in Akamai’s history. The company said capital spending tied to this one agreement will total about $5.5 billion.
That figure is more than six times what Akamai spent on capital expenditures in all of 2025.
The new contract builds on an earlier deal. Akamai and Anthropic struck a $1.8 billion computing agreement earlier this year.
Akamai also announced more than $2.8 billion in other multi year cloud infrastructure commitments this year. The Anthropic deal adds to that total.
Anthropic has been seeking more computing power as demand grows. Customers have been using its Claude software for coding and other tasks.
The AI company has signed deals with several other providers this year. These include Google and SpaceX for access to chips and computing capacity.
As part of the agreement, Akamai issued a warrant to Anthropic. The warrant allows Anthropic to buy Series B preferred shares at $111.33 each.
Those shares convert into 7.7 million shares of common stock. That represents up to about 5% of Akamai’s outstanding common stock.
About 2% of that stock is expected to vest along with the $11.6 billion commitment. The rest could vest if Anthropic expands its spending by up to $9 billion more over the contract term.
Each additional $3 billion in cloud services purchased would vest about 1% more stock.
This marks the first time Akamai has agreed to issue a warrant as part of a cloud deal with a customer. Chief Executive Tom Leighton called it a serious step.
Leighton said the arrangement made sense because it helps bring the two companies closer together.
Akamai generates most of its revenue from content delivery and cybersecurity services. The company has been expanding into computing to find new sources of growth.
Leighton said the cloud business is growing fast. He said revenue from cloud contracts could soon pass sales from the company’s other segments.
Akamai expects revenue from the Anthropic business to reach between $150 million and $300 million next year. By 2028, the company expects an annual run rate of about $1.7 billion from the deal.
The bulk of Akamai’s related capital spending will go toward hardware such as servers, chips and networking equipment. Most of that spending is expected to happen next year.
Akamai said it does not expect the deal to affect its 2026 revenue guidance. The company does expect a capital expenditure increase of about $1.7 billion in 2026 tied to supply chain components including memory.
Leighton said Akamai is in talks about additional business with other major technology companies. He said this includes large data center operators and big enterprises.
The computing agreement is expected to begin in the second half of next year.

pages.text:
Akamai expands deal to $11.6 billion partnership with Anthropic
As part of the largest deal in company history, Akamai will provide cloud services to the AI company over the next seven years
The main lobby at Akamai's headquarters in Kendall Square on Oct. 29, 2019.Suzanne Kreiter/Globe staff/file
Akamai Technologies in Cambridge announced an $11.6 billion deal with Anthropic on Thursday, providing cloud services to the artificial intelligence company over the next seven years.
The move is the latest chapter in a partnership between one of the fastest growing AI companies and the dot-com era innovator. The deal is the largest contract in Akamai’s history, according to Tom Leighton, chief executive.
Leighton said the deal helps position Akamai to be, “the infrastructure provider for the next generation of AI powered applications.”
“We are building upon our global footprint and years of experience in serving the world’s largest enterprises to enable and secure responsible AI,” Leighton said on a company conference call.
In May, Akamai’s share price soared after it announced a $1.8 billion deal with a “leading frontier model provider.” At the time, neither company would confirm it was with Anthropic, but SEC filings confirm the businesses signed an agreement on May 5.
The announcement Thursday expanded the relationship to $11.6 billion, with the potential for an additional $9 billion in revenue commitments, which would bring the total deal to roughly $20 billion, said Ed McGowan, the chief financial officer of Akamai.
Akamai’s stock did not jump as high as it did in May (trading then at $160) but still rose to a high of $135 following the announcement.
Akamai will spend $5.5 billion over the next two years to support the deal and does not anticipate generating revenue from the contract in 2026. Earnings of $150 to $300 million are expected to come in the second half of 2027, said McGowan, and are expected to continue to increase through 2028. After that, Akamai estimates $1.7 billion in revenue annually.
Akamai also issued a warrant to Anthropic to purchase 7.7 million shares of its common stock, which is approximately a five percent stake.
Leighton said customers are using Akamai’s cloud services to support a variety of applications, many of which are now powered by AI. Examples he gave included customer service voice agents, translation services, speech recognition for subtitles, robotics and simulation renderings.

Anthropic has been working with multiple suppliers this year to secure computing resources. In July, it signed a 20-year lease with TeraWulf to secure about 401 megawatts at the Hosville data centre in Kentucky. In June, it signed a memory and storage supply contract with Micron.

Should You Stay Cautious About AKAM Stock Despite AI Cloud Momentum?
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 8:07 AM PDT 4 min read
Akamai Technologies Inc. AKAM is increasingly transforming itself from a traditional content delivery network provider into a cybersecurity and cloud infrastructure player. Solid security demand, rapid growth in Cloud Infrastructure Services (CIS) and rising exposure to artificial intelligence (AI) workloads support its long-term prospects.
However, declining profitability, persistent weakness in the delivery business and significantly higher infrastructure investments suggest that investors should remain cautious about the stock.
Security Business & Cloud Infrastructure: Key Growth Avenues
Akamai's security portfolio continues to provide stability to the overall business. Second-quarter 2026 security revenues increased 10% year over year to $604 million and accounted for more than half of total revenues. Growing demand for application security, API protection and protection against increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks should support this segment over the long run.
Cloud Infrastructure Services is emerging as one of Akamai's fastest-growing businesses. CIS revenues surged 39% year over year to $99 million in the second quarter. Through the first half of 2026, Akamai signed several multi-year CIS contracts with an aggregate value of more than $2.8 billion. The expanding contract pipeline indicates growing customer acceptance of Akamai's distributed cloud platform.
Anthropic Deal Strengthens AI Opportunity
Akamai's expanded relationship with Anthropic significantly enhances its exposure to AI infrastructure demand. Anthropic committed $11.6 billion over seven years to utilize Akamai's distributed cloud infrastructure, with the potential for the agreement to expand by an additional $9 billion.
The deal provides solid long-term revenue visibility and validates Akamai's strategy of positioning its infrastructure closer to workloads and end users.
Delivery Business & Margin Contraction: Major Concerns
Despite strength in security and cloud, Akamai's legacy delivery operations remain a drag. Revenues from delivery and other cloud applications declined 6% year over year to roughly $396 million in the second quarter. Continued erosion in this business could offset part of the growth generated by newer cloud offerings.
Akamai's profitability trends are also less encouraging. Second-quarter revenues increased 5% year over year to $1.1 billion, but non-GAAP earnings declined 8% to $1.59 per share. Adjusted EBITDA fell 6%, while non-GAAP operating margin contracted to 25% from 30% in the year-ago quarter.
The divergence between revenue growth and earnings performance highlights the increasing cost burden associated with Akamai's ongoing transformation.
The company's AI infrastructure expansion requires substantial capital investment. Akamai expects approximately $5.5 billion of total capital expenditures related to the Anthropic commitment, including around $1.7 billion of incremental capex in 2026.
Capital intensity was high even before the expanded Anthropic agreement. Second-quarter capital expenditures totaled $347 million, representing approximately 32% of revenues compared with 21% in the prior-year period. Sustained elevated spending could weigh on free cash flow and returns on invested capital, particularly if cloud capacity utilization ramps more slowly than expected.
Akamai declined 5% over the past six months against the industry's growth of 14.2%. It has underperformed peers like trivago N.V. TRVG and Sprout Social, Inc. SPT. While TRVG has gained 59.7%, SPT jumped 74.5% during this period.
2026 Outlook Offers Limited Near-Term Upside
Management currently expects 2026 revenues between $4.45 billion and $4.53 billion. While security and cloud growth should support the top line, continued delivery weakness and elevated infrastructure expenses could restrict meaningful earnings expansion in the near term.
Earnings estimates for AKAM for 2026 have moved down 4.6% to $6.62 over the past year, while the same for 2027 has decreased 8.6% to $6.79. The negative estimate revision depicts bearish sentiment about the stock's growth potential.
Should Investors Buy AKAM Stock?
Akamai's long-term strategic direction remains encouraging. Cybersecurity demand is healthy, CIS is expanding rapidly and the Anthropic partnership significantly strengthens the company's position in AI infrastructure.
However, the investment case is accompanied by meaningful risks. With declining earnings estimates, the stock is witnessing negative investor sentiment. Margin compression, declining earnings, delivery weakness and sharply rising capital requirements could limit upside until the benefits of Akamai's cloud investments become more visible.
With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), AKAM appears to be treading in the middle of the road, and new investors could be better off if they trade with caution. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Resurety and Akamai Make Clean Energy History With First-Ever Exchange-Executed VPPA
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 7:00 AM PDT 5 min read
BOSTON, September 30, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Boston-area based cybersecurity and cloud computing company Akamai Technologies completed the first-ever clean energy transaction executed on a CFTC-registered exchange by securing a new high-impact solar Virtual Power Purchase Agreement (VPPA) on August 31, 2026 on Resurety's CleanTrade marketplace. This milestone reinforces Akamai's commitment to its 2030 goal of reaching net-zero emissions across its global platform and operations.
Resurety's CleanTrade platform is the first and only marketplace registered with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) for transacting clean energy on an as-produced basis. Resurety, also Boston-based, provides market intelligence, portfolio software, consulting, and a regulated marketplace to empower clean energy buyers, sellers, and investors.
This VPPA transaction marks a turning point in how corporate clean energy is bought and sold, proving that clean energy procurement does not need to be a slow, opaque process:
Speed: CleanTrade gives buyers instant access to a live exchange of active market offers, allowing Akamai to discover a viable deal that would have been missed in their standard RFP process. By leveraging Resurety's embedded carbon analytics, Akamai evaluated the project's real-world emissionality, aligning the transaction with their consequential climate framework, "CLIMATE- 2026". Direct, on-platform negotiation of key terms significantly reduced deal friction, leading Mike Mattera, Akamai's Global Head of Corporate Sustainability and ESG Officer, to call it "the fastest VPPA Akamai has ever completed."
Trust: Procuring on a regulated marketplace with pre-vetted developers and bids reduced counterparty concerns. Resurety's robust pre- and post-trade analytics also mitigated guesswork, uncertainty, and questions commonly associated with clean energy transactions.
Simplicity: The CleanTrade platform delivers everything needed to research, execute, and manage the transaction in one place. By integrating pre-transaction market analytics and post-transaction settlement tracking through Resurety's CleanSight Manage feature, Mattera coined CleanTrade 'the easy-button for clean energy procurement.'
Historically, purchasing clean energy without a centralized exchange meant navigating a slow RFP process, disconnected spreadsheets, lengthy email chains, and drawn-out negotiations. Limited to proposals within a buyer's immediate network, companies also had no reliable way to verify fair, competitive market pricing.
Furthermore, traditional annual volumetric matching often masked true grid carbon impact. Through this transaction, Akamai is operationalizing its consequential procurement philosophy — moving past check-the-box accounting to prioritize emissionality, investing where new clean power displaces the highest amount of carbon on the grid.
Akamai selected an Indiana-based solar project for its high carbon abatement potential relative to the local grid. The almost 200MW project is expected to generate over 400,000 MWh annually. Because Indiana's grid relies more heavily on fossil fuels, every MWh of clean energy produced there displaces approximately 540 kg of CO2 per MWh. By contrast, projects in regions with higher renewable penetration, such as Texas (ERCOT), displace around 350 kg of CO2 per MWh.
CleanTrade's regulated, digital marketplace evolves clean energy procurement into a transparent, real-time market that is accessible to all qualified buyers. As Resurety's Co-Founder and CEO Lee Taylor puts it, "For too long, the complexity and opacity of clean energy procurement kept transaction costs high and left high-impact VPPAs out of reach for all but the largest clean energy buyers. CleanTrade changes that dynamic completely. By bringing market transparency, standardized terms and underwriting, and compliance confidence through an exchange environment, we're removing common friction points and empowering corporate buyers of every scale to execute deals quickly, deploy capital efficiently, and drive real decarbonization."
"We're on a mission to reach net-zero and power Akamai's global platform with 100% renewable energy by 2030, and we are determined to do it by putting truly clean energy onto the grid. Resurety's CleanTrade gave us the transparency and speed we needed to close the fastest VPPA in our history. This is about moving past promises and taking the kind of urgent, consequential action our planet needs right now," stresses Mattera. With Akamai set to leverage CleanTrade for additional VPPA transactions, the future of energy procurement is here. Together, the two Boston-area companies are empowering buyers to invest in clean energy, work toward their impact goals, and accelerate the transition to a zero-carbon future.

Through our industry-leading market intelligence and portfolio management software, our expert consulting services, and the leading regulated clean energy marketplace, we deliver the infrastructure and information needed to move the entire industry – and your business – forward. Resurety's CleanTrade™ is the first and only CFTC-registered transaction platform for as-generated energy, and our CleanSight™ software simplifies complex workflows with the most sophisticated intelligence and portfolio management tools in the market. The result is increased transparency, liquidity, speed, and impact for the industry and for your business. To learn more, visit resurety.com, view our intelligence resources or follow us on LinkedIn.

This move reflects a structural shift in the industry, where securing decentralized computing infrastructure—independent of traditional single-cloud providers—has become essential to meet the explosively growing computational demands of AI models.
The Full Scope of the $11.6 Billion Mega-Deal Between Akamai and Anthropic
Overview of the Agreement and Key Highlights
On September 24, 2026, U.S. cloud giant Akamai Technologies announced that it had signed a seven-year, $11.6 billion (approximately 1.7 trillion yen) cloud infrastructure agreement with AI development leader Anthropic. This contract is one of the largest commercial transactions in Akamai's history, supporting Anthropic's surging CPU workloads and large-scale computational processing needs through Akamai's decentralized cloud platform, "Akamai Cloud." Furthermore, the agreement includes a contract expansion clause of up to $9 billion, potentially bringing the total transaction value to approximately $20 billion. Regarding the impact on financial performance, while there is no change to the full-year 2026 revenue guidance, service delivery is scheduled to begin sequentially from the second half of 2027. According to Dr. Tom Leighton, co-founder and CEO of Akamai, the company expects a revenue contribution of $150 million to $300 million in 2027, growing to an annual run rate of approximately $1.7 billion by 2028. Akamai had already secured over $2.8 billion in cloud infrastructure contracts in 2026, but this deal solidifies its position as an AI infrastructure provider.
Granting of Stock Warrants and Deep Collaboration in Both Capital and Business
An extremely unusual feature of this agreement is the strong capital tie-up accompanying the transaction. Akamai has granted Anthropic warrants (stock acquisition rights) for non-voting convertible Series B preferred stock, which can be converted into up to approximately 7.7 million shares of common stock (equivalent to about 5% of issued common shares) at an exercise price of $111.33 per share. Approximately 2% of the warrants vested immediately in connection with the initial $11.6 billion commitment, with the remaining 3% vesting in stages based on additional service purchases (approximately 1% for every $3 billion). This is the first time in Akamai's 28-year history that a cloud provider has issued stock warrants to a customer. CEO Tom Leighton stated that this is a meaningful step toward deepening the long-term, strategic partnership between the two companies. While market analysts have praised this capital alliance as a sign of high confidence in the sustainability of AI demand, there is also interest in the circular nature of the transaction, where AI companies and infrastructure firms hold each other's capital and business. Surging Demand for Generative AI and Structural Shift to Decentralized Infrastructure
Background of Anthropic's Explosive Growth and Securing Compute Resources
The backdrop to Anthropic's series of massive infrastructure deals is the staggering growth in demand for its "Claude" AI model. According to CEO Dario Amodei, the company's annualized revenue recorded an exceptional 80-fold year-on-year growth in the first quarter of 2026, reaching a run-rate revenue of $47 billion (approximately 7 trillion yen) as of May 2026. Additionally, in its Series H round in May 2026, the company raised $65 billion, pushing its valuation to $965 billion, nearly reaching the $1 trillion mark. With this rapid increase in usage, a severe shortage of computational resources has become a challenge, and the company has been scrambling to secure large-scale compute resources to maintain its model training and inference environments. In 2026, the company has been aggressively pursuing multi-billion dollar infrastructure procurement, including a $10 billion deal with Volta, a $13.7 billion deal with Lam Group, the leasing of the entire capacity of the Colossus 1 data center operated by xAI, and a partnership with Amazon (AWS) exceeding $100 billion and 5 gigawatts.
Breaking Away from Dependence on Traditional Hyperscalers and Moving Toward Multi-Cloud
Anthropic's infrastructure procurement strategy marks a clear departure from the "dependence on a specific single hyperscaler" seen in traditional frontier AI development companies. The company has now built a multi-provider system combining the "Big Three"—Amazon (AWS), Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure—along with xAI's Colossus 1 and Akamai. In particular, the adoption of Akamai, which possesses over 4,300 edge locations in 135 countries worldwide, enables low-latency inference processing and distributed execution of CPU workloads in edge environments scattered across the globe. Especially in enterprise sectors with high regulatory requirements such as law, finance, and healthcare, it is necessary to meet data residency (restrictions on data storage regions) and cybersecurity requirements, where Akamai's decentralized infrastructure plays a crucial role. This multi-cloud structure, which allows for business continuity even if a single massive cloud experiences outages or regulatory changes, has become a source of competitive advantage in the enterprise AI market.
Ripple Effects on the Entire Industry and the Future of AI Infrastructure
Stock Market Evaluation and Akamai's Large-Scale Capital Expenditure Plan
Following the announcement of the mega-deal, the stock market reacted very favorably to Akamai's business transformation. In after-hours trading immediately following the announcement, Akamai's stock price (AKAM) surged by 20% to 22%, jumping from its previous level of $110.41 to around $133.50. To fulfill the contract, Akamai expects capital expenditure (CapEx) of approximately $5.5 billion against the initial $11.6 billion commitment. For 2026 alone, the company raised its capital expenditure forecast by approximately $1.7 billion to pre-purchase critical components such as memory, issued a $1.7 billion construction request to major electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider Jabil, and completed a hardware procurement agreement with Lenovo. Physical infrastructure construction is already well underway.
The Rise of Edge-Based AI Computing Platforms and Future Outlook
This agreement symbolizes the arrival of a major trend in the future AI infrastructure market: "from centralized data centers to edge-distributed computing platforms." With the spread of agentic AI that autonomously executes inferences and tasks, demand for low-latency processing at network endpoints and distributed computing with high CPU loads is expected to increase further. The biggest point of focus for future developments is the pace of progress in service delivery and monetization, which will begin in earnest from the second half of 2027. The focus will be on whether Akamai can smoothly achieve its target annual revenue run rate of $1.7 billion by 2028, and whether the additional $9 billion contract expansion option will be exercised. As the fusion of centralized hyperscalers and decentralized edge clouds progresses, the horizon of AI infrastructure is entering a new phase of growth.

The agreement will supply Anthropic with central processing units. These are general purpose chips used to help run AI software.
Akamai shares jumped as much as 20% in after hours trading following the news. The stock rose to roughly $129.60 per share.

The new contract builds on an earlier deal. Akamai and Anthropic struck a $1.8 billion computing agreement earlier this year.

The computing agreement is expected to begin in the second half of next year.

Should You Stay Cautious About AKAM Stock Despite AI Cloud Momentum?
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 8:07 AM PDT 4 min read
Akamai Technologies Inc. AKAM is increasingly transforming itself from a traditional content delivery network provider into a cybersecurity and cloud infrastructure player. Solid security demand, rapid growth in Cloud Infrastructure Services (CIS) and rising exposure to artificial intelligence (AI) workloads support its long-term prospects.
However, declining profitability, persistent weakness in the delivery business and significantly higher infrastructure investments suggest that investors should remain cautious about the stock.
Security Business & Cloud Infrastructure: Key Growth Avenues
Akamai's security portfolio continues to provide stability to the overall business. Second-quarter 2026 security revenues increased 10% year over year to $604 million and accounted for more than half of total revenues. Growing demand for application security, API protection and protection against increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks should support this segment over the long run.
